body.statement:
Let \(k,r\in\mathbb N_0\), let \(\mu\) be a probability law on \(\mathbb R^k\), and write \(	au_h\mu\) for its translate by \(h\in\mathbb R^k\).  If \(	au_h\mu=\mu\), then \(h=0\).  Consequently, if linear maps \(T,T':\mathbb R^r	o\mathbb R^k\) and probability laws \(\mu,
u\) satisfy \(	au_{Tx}\mu=	au_{T'x}
u\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^r\), then \(\mu=
u\) and \(T=T'\).
body.proof_tex:
The assertion is immediate for \(k=0\), so suppose \(k>0\).  Let
\[
 \phi_\mu(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^k}e^{\mathrm i t^{\mathsf T}z}\,d\mu(z).
\]
We first verify directly that \(\phi_\mu(t)\to1\) as \(t\to0\).  Given \(\eta>0\), continuity from below applied to the balls \(\{\lVert z\rVert\le R\}\) gives an \(R<\infty\) with \(\mu\{\lVert z\rVert>R\}<\eta\).  Since \(|e^{\mathrm i u}-1|\le |u|\),
\[
 |\phi_\mu(t)-1|
 \le \lVert t\rVert R+2\eta.
\]
Thus \(\phi_\mu\) is nonzero throughout some neighborhood of the origin.

If \(\tau_h\mu=\mu\), the characteristic functions obey
\[
 e^{\mathrm i t^{\mathsf T}h}\phi_\mu(t)=\phi_\mu(t).
\]
Were \(h\ne0\), one could choose \(t=ch\) with \(c>0\) so small that \(t\) lies in that neighborhood and \(0<c\lVert h\rVert^2<2\pi\).  The displayed equality would then give \(e^{\mathrm i c\lVert h\rVert^2}=1\), a contradiction.  Hence \(h=0\).

For the consequence, taking \(x=0\) gives \(\mu=\nu\).  Translating the asserted equality by \(-T'x\) shows that \(\mu\) is invariant under \((T-T')x\).  The first part gives \((T-T')x=0\) for every \(x\), so \(T=T'\).
